Card text: what the every-minute job does: returns snoozed mail, seals mail that waited for its owner to set up keys, converts old unencrypted mail from the single-user version; and (new) applies two-factor resets that are due (an admin's reset of another admin waits 24 hours) and, seven days after a person asked, deletes their locked old mail (mail sealed to a key that was replaced).

docs.arch_d1.context: CAT-22. Card text: what is stored in D1, and what is NOT encrypted there. "Sealed" = encrypted so that only the owner can read it. The mail index keeps sender, recipients, dates, sizes and labels readable (unencrypted); subject, text and attachment names are encrypted. Keep both halves.

docs.arch_d1_title.context: Card title: D1 is the name of Cloudflare's SQLite database product; never translated.

"Sealed to that person's key" = encrypted so that only that person can open it; keep the glossary words for sealing and key. DATA_KEY is the name of a server secret: keep it as it is. An address with no account is rejected.

docs.arch_inbound_title.context: Card title in the Architecture tab: how incoming mail is received.

docs.arch_keys.context: Card text. {data_key} is the name of a secret (never translated). It protects what the server must read back itself, including mail that arrives before its owner has set up keys.

docs.arch_keys_title.context: Card title in the Architecture tab: how keys and secrets are used.

docs.arch_outbound.context: CAT-20. Card text. Mail to other servers goes out through Cloudflare Email Sending. Mail between two people on this same deployment is encrypted in the sender's browser and stays inside, BUT ONLY when every recipient has set up encryption keys and the message is within the size limits; otherwise the server can read it (a copy for a person without keys is sent unencrypted to the server; a message that is too large goes out through Email Sending and comes back in). Keep both conditions and both exceptions (do not call it "end-to-end encrypted" here: that term is for the badge only).

forgot.lead.context: Under the heading: what the three steps are.

forgot.nothing_changed.context: Reassurance on the new-recovery-key screen: nothing on the server has changed until the person confirms the key.

forgot.password_lead.context: Under the heading: the recovery key was accepted.

forgot.password_title.context: Heading of step 2 of the forgotten-password flow.

forgot.title.context: Heading of the forgotten-password page (step 1 of 3).

frame.images_blocked.context: Bar above an HTML message that has remote images, left of the 'Show images' button

frame.title.context: Accessible title of the frame that shows the HTML body of a message (screen readers only)

gate.continue.context: Button: moves to the next step of a first-sign-in screen.

gate.current_password_lead.context: When the page was reloaded in the middle of the first sign-in: ask once for the temporary password again.

gate.keys_lead.context: Under the heading of the key setup screen.

gate.keys_title.context: Heading of the screen that sets up the encryption keys and shows the recovery key.

gate.new_password.context: Label of the new password field.

gate.password_lead.context: Under the heading: the account is still on the temporary password an admin made; choose your own.

gate.password_title.context: Heading of the first-sign-in screen that asks for a new password.

gate.passwords_differ.context: The two new passwords typed are not equal.

gate.repeat_password.context: Label of the field that repeats the new password.

gate.two_factor_lead.context: Under the heading of the two-factor setup screen: it is required for this account.

gate.two_factor_title.context: Heading of the screen that sets up two-factor sign-in at first sign-in.

keys.open_failed.context: The keys could not be opened with the typed password (wrong password, or damaged keys): shown on the unlock screen and after a sign-in whose keys do not open.

keys.unlock.context: Button: unlocks the encryption key with the typed password.

keys.unlock_lead.context: Under the unlock heading. {address} is the person's email address.

keys.unlock_title.context: Heading of the unlock screen: signed in, but this browser has no key (reload on a shared device, or the stored key expired).

lang.label.context: Label of the language list in Settings and in the admin console

lang.not_loaded.context: Error under the language list when the chosen language file could not be fetched (offline)

lang.org_default.context: Label of the organisation's default language in the admin console

lang.org_default_hint.context: Help text under the organisation default language list

lang.picker_label.context: Screen-reader name of the small language list on the sign-in screens (no visible label)

list.attachment.context: Small chip on a message row that has an attachment (singular)

list.draft_to.context: Row title of a draft: who it is addressed to; {recipients} is one or more email addresses

list.empty_in.context: Empty-state title of a folder; {folder} is the folder name (Inbox, Sent, a label name)

list.filter_all.context: Filter chip above the message list: show all messages

list.filter_unread.context: Filter chip above the message list: show only unread messages

list.group_earlier.context: Heading of the group of older messages (shown in capitals)

list.group_later.context: Snoozed folder heading: messages that come back after more than 7 days (shown in capitals)

list.group_next_7_days.context: Snoozed folder heading: messages that come back within the next 7 days (shown in capitals)

list.group_this_week.context: Heading of the group of messages from earlier this week (shown in capitals)

list.group_today.context: Heading of the group of messages from today (shown in capitals)

list.group_tomorrow.context: Snoozed folder heading: messages that come back tomorrow (shown in capitals)

list.group_yesterday.context: Heading of the group of messages from yesterday (shown in capitals)

list.has_attachments.context: Screen-reader label of the paperclip icon on a mobile message row

list.hint_clear_filter.context: Empty-state second line when a filter and a search match nothing; All is the name of the All filter chip

list.hint_inbox.context: Empty Inbox (and any other folder without its own text), second line

list.hint_label.context: Empty folder of a user label, second line

list.hint_switch_all.context: Empty-state second line when a filter matches nothing; All is the name of the All filter chip

list.load_failed.context: Empty-state title when the message list could not be loaded

list.load_failed_hint.context: Empty-state second line when the message list could not be loaded

list.load_more.context: Button at the end of the message list that loads older messages

list.loading.context: Shown in the middle of the list while the first page of messages loads

list.mark_all_read.context: Icon button above the message list, tooltip and screen-reader label

list.no_match.context: Empty-state title when a filter chip matches nothing

list.no_match_search.context: Empty-state title when a filter chip and a search together match nothing

list.no_recipient.context: Row title of a draft that has no recipient yet (Drafts folder)

list.no_results.context: Empty-state title of a search with no result; {query} is what the person typed

list.no_subject.context: Row title for a message with an empty subject

list.refresh.context: Icon button above the message list, tooltip and screen-reader label

list.star_from.context: Screen-reader label of the star button on a message row; {sender} is the sender name or address

list.try_other_search.context: Empty-state second line after a search with no result

list.unread_sr.context: Screen-reader only text before an unread message row

locked.banner#one.context: Card above the mailbox, singular ({count} is 1). After an admin restored their account with the setup key, mail that arrived before is sealed to the OLD encryption key, which is gone, so nobody can open it. Calm, factual; two buttons follow (Keep, Delete). Glossary: message, key, encrypt.

locked.cancel.context: Button that stops a deletion of locked old mail that was asked for and is waiting for its date (on the locked-mail card and on the notice). vi and zh-CN are cyber's (overrides); no need to translate.

locked.confirm_label.context: Label of the field in the confirmation dialog where the person types their own email address, which is shown in the label ({address}), so a stray click cannot start the deletion.

locked.delete.context: Button on the locked-mail card that opens the confirmation, and the red button of that confirmation (title: Delete locked mail). It does not delete at once.

locked.dialog_body#one.context: First line of the confirmation dialog, singular. Deleted locked mail cannot be brought back.

locked.dialog_note.context: Plain note under the first line of the confirmation dialog: the server waits several days before deleting, and the person can cancel in that time. Do not write the number of days.

locked.dialog_title.context: Title of the confirmation dialog that asks for the address, the password and (with two-factor sign-in) the authenticator code before locked messages are scheduled for deletion.

locked.keep.context: Button on the locked-mail card: leave the locked messages where they are and put the card away for now. Nothing is sent to the server.

locked.not_pending.context: Second line of the notice about a requested deletion of locked mail, shown when the deletion is not waiting any more (the person cancelled it, or it has been carried out).

locked.pending#one.context: Card above the mailbox while a deletion of locked mail waits for its date, singular. {date} is a date and time; the person can cancel until then (Cancel deletion button next to it).

locked.region.context: Landmark label (read by screen readers) of the card above the mailbox that tells the person that some old messages are locked.

login.signing_in.context: Label of the sign-in button while the password is being checked

mailcrypto.download_raw.context: Button: text button at the bottom of the reader that saves the original message as an .eml file.

mailcrypto.images_hidden.context: Line above the mail frame in the reader when the message has pictures embedded in it (not remote ones) and the person has not chosen Show images yet; the Show images button sits next to it.

mailcrypto.note_failed.context: Reader body when a message arrived but could not be opened in the browser (damaged data or an unexpected format).

mailcrypto.note_locked.context: Reader body when no key is unlocked in the browser yet, so no message can be opened.

mailcrypto.note_other_key.context: Reader body for a message that was encrypted to a key other than the one now in use (for example after an admin recovery of the account). Says only what this browser can do; it does not claim who else can or cannot open it.

mailcrypto.note_pending.context: Reader body for a message that arrived before the person had a key and has not been sealed to their key yet.

mailcrypto.subject_failed.context: Shown in place of the subject (list row and reader heading) for a message that could not be opened.

mailcrypto.subject_locked.context: Shown in place of the subject (list row and reader heading) for a message that is locked: no key unlocked yet, or sealed to another key.

mailcrypto.subject_pending.context: Shown in place of the subject (list row and reader heading) for a message still being prepared for the person's key.

notice.cancel_reset.context: Button on the notice about a pending reset of the person's two-factor sign-in: stops the reset.

notice.dismiss.context: Button on a notice in the banner: hides it for good.

notice.dismiss_later.context: Shown under a notice that cannot be dismissed yet: security notices stay for seven days. {date} is a date and time.

notice.more.context: Button (link style) under the banner when there are more than three notices: opens Settings, Account tab, where all of them are listed.

notice.region.context: Accessible name of the banner above the mailbox that lists account notices. Read by screen readers only.

password.check_failed.context: Password field status line (red alert) when the data of the common-password check could not be loaded; a Try again link follows it.

password.check_loading.context: Password field status line with a spinner while the data of the common-password check loads.

password.hide.context: Button (icon only): crossed-eye icon inside the password field that hides the typed password again; aria-label, no visible text.

password.level_fair.context: Password strength result shown under the password field (second level) and spoken by the strength meter.

password.level_good.context: Password strength result shown under the password field (third level) and spoken by the strength meter.

password.level_strong.context: Password strength result shown under the password field (highest level) and spoken by the strength meter.

password.level_weak.context: Password strength result shown under the password field (lowest level; also the level of a refused password) and spoken by the strength meter.

password.meter_empty.context: Screen reader value of the password strength bar while the field is empty (aria-valuetext). Not shown on screen.

password.meter_label.context: Screen reader name of the password strength bar (aria-label of the meter under the password field). Not shown on screen.

password.problem_common.context: Password field status line: the password is on the lists of common passwords (also with digits, symbols or look-alike letters added).

password.problem_has_account_word.context: Password field status line: the password contains a word taken from the account's address, domain or display name.

password.problem_predictable.context: Password field status line: the strength estimate finds the password too easy to guess (repeats, runs such as abc or 1234, keyboard rows, one common word).

password.problem_too_long.context: Password field status line: the password is longer than allowed. {max} = the maximum length (256).

password.problem_too_short#one.context: Password field status line while typing: the password is too short, one character is missing. {count} = characters still missing, {min} = the minimum for this account.

password.problem_too_short#other.context: Password field status line while typing: the password is too short. {count} = characters still missing, {min} = the minimum for this account.

password.rules.context: Password field status line while nothing is typed: the password rules, fixed by the Product Owner. {min} = minimum length for members (12), {adminMin} = minimum length for admins (16); both are numbers from constants.

password.show.context: Button (icon only): eye icon inside the password field that shows the typed password; aria-label, no visible text.

password.suggest.context: Button under the password field on admin screens: fills in a generated passphrase (random words) and shows it. Shown with a wand icon.

password.suggest_another.context: Button under the password field on admin screens, after a passphrase was suggested: generates a different one. Shown with a wand icon.

password.suggest_hint.context: Hint shown under the Suggest button after a passphrase was filled in. {words} = how many random words the passphrase has (a number, 6).

push.blocked.context: Settings > Notifications error when the browser has notifications blocked for this site

push.dev_server.context: Settings > Notifications error in a development build, where the service worker is not registered

push.device_off_failed.context: Settings > Notifications error when turning notifications off on this device did not work

push.device_unknown.context: Settings > Notifications error after Send test: the push service dropped this device

push.no_device.context: Settings > Notifications error after Send test: no device is registered

push.not_allowed.context: Settings > Notifications error when the browser permission prompt was dismissed without an answer

push.service_rejected.context: Settings > Notifications error after Send test: the push service refused the notification

push.service_unreachable.context: Settings > Notifications error when the browser cannot reach its push service (e.g. Google, Apple, Mozilla)

push.test_failed.context: Settings > Notifications fallback error for Send test

push.turn_off_failed.context: Settings > Notifications fallback error for turning notifications off

push.turn_on_failed.context: Settings > Notifications fallback error for turning notifications on

reader.add_label.context: Reader toolbar: aria-label and tooltip of the icon button that opens the label menu. Icon-only: no visible text.

reader.arrived_by_email.context: A quiet chip above the text of a received message that arrived over email from outside (not sent between people of this deployment) while its From address is one of THIS deployment's own domains: anyone on the internet can write such an address, so the app says nobody checked it. Neutral colour, not an alarm; it does not say the message is fake.

reader.attachments_summary#one.context: Reader attachments heading, one file: {count} is 1, {size} is the total size such as "12 KB".

reader.attachments_summary#other.context: Reader attachments heading, several files: {count} files, {size} is the total size such as "1.2 MB".

reader.back_to_list.context: Reader toolbar, phone only: aria-label of the icon button that goes back to the message list (tooltip is common.back). Icon-only: no visible text, tooltip/screen reader.

reader.create_label.context: Label menu: aria-label and tooltip of the round + button that creates the typed label. Icon-only.

reader.download.context: Reader attachments: tooltip of the download icon on each attachment row.

reader.download_file.context: Reader attachments: aria-label of the download icon of one attachment; {name} is the file name. Screen reader only.

reader.label_added.context: Label menu: small marker at the right of a label that is already on the open message, inside a 240 px menu row.

reader.label_exists.context: Label menu: red hint when a label with that name already exists (case-insensitive).

reader.label_invalid.context: Label menu: red hint under the new-label field when the name has a character that is not allowed (letters, numbers, space, - and _ are allowed).

reader.label_limit.context: Label menu: red hint when the message already has the most labels it may have. {max} is a fixed number (20).

reader.label_name_limit.context: Label menu: grey hint under the new-label field once the name has reached the longest allowed length. {max} is a fixed number (30).

reader.loading_message.context: Reader pane while the open message loads (spinner and text).

reader.new_label.context: Label menu: placeholder and aria-label of the field where a new label name is typed (about 170 px wide, 16 px font).

reader.newer.context: Reader toolbar (desktop): tooltip of the icon button that opens the next newer message.

reader.newer_message.context: Reader toolbar (desktop): aria-label of the icon button that opens the next newer message. Screen reader only.

reader.no_subject.context: Reader heading when the message has no subject.

reader.none_selected.context: Reader pane title when no message is open (under the Edgar picture).

reader.none_selected_hint.context: Reader pane hint under the empty-state title.

reader.older.context: Reader toolbar (desktop): tooltip of the icon button that opens the next older message.

reader.older_message.context: Reader toolbar (desktop): aria-label of the icon button that opens the next older message. Screen reader only.

reader.to_cc_line.context: Reader sender block, grey line when the message also has copy recipients: {to} and {cc} are addresses or lists of addresses.

reader.to_line.context: Reader sender block, grey line under the sender name: who the message was sent to. {to} is an address or a list of addresses. Lowercase on purpose (it reads like "to me").

reader.view_html.context: Reader: segmented switch above the body (shown only when the message has both forms): formatted (HTML) version. Technical word, may stay "HTML".

reader.view_plain.context: Reader: segmented switch above the body: plain-text version of the message.

recovery.claim.context: The one security sentence on every recovery-key screen and inside the downloaded file. Exact claim of the design (15.1): nobody, admins included, can restore mail without the password or the recovery key.

recovery.confirm_button.context: Button: the person confirms they saved the recovery key; this sends the request that stores the keys.

recovery.confirm_lead.context: Asks the person to type back three groups of the key to show they saved it. {first}, {second} and {third} are group numbers (1 to 9, never neighbours).

recovery.confirm_mismatch.context: The typed groups were wrong; the next attempt asks for different groups.

recovery.copy_failed.context: Shown when the browser refused to copy the recovery key to the clipboard.

recovery.download.context: Button: saves the recovery key as a text file (secondary button next to Copy).

recovery.download_warning.context: Warning under the Copy and Download buttons: a downloaded file stays on the device; on iPhone and iPad the file opens in a viewer, so Copy is the way there.

recovery.file_title.context: First line of the downloaded recovery key text file. {address} is the person's email address. The product name stays as it is.

recovery.group_label.context: Small label above each of the nine groups of six characters of the recovery key, and above each box of the typed check. {number} is 1 to 9.

recovery.old_stops.context: Shown only when the new key replaces an earlier one: the old recovery key stops working ON THIS SERVER at once when the person finishes. The scope matters (PB-11): the mail key does not change, so an old copy of the stored data plus the old recovery key would still open old mail; do not translate it as "stops working" without "on this server".

recovery.problem_characters.context: Typed recovery key containing a character that is not part of the key alphabet.

recovery.problem_checksum.context: Typed recovery key whose two check characters do not match: a typing mistake, found before anything is sent.

recovery.problem_length.context: Typed recovery key with the wrong number of characters (54 in nine groups of six, hyphens and spaces ignored).

recovery.shown_once.context: Under the claim: the key is displayed one time only.

recovery.title_first.context: Heading of the screen that shows the recovery key for the first time (first sign-in, first-run setup).

recovery.title_new.context: Heading of the screen that shows a NEW recovery key (after 'Create a new recovery key' and after a forgotten-password recovery).

security.admin_claim_no_access.context: First sentence of the admin claim, shown where an admin role is chosen or confirmed and on the first-run Setup screen. Final wording from the Product Owner (addendum 4.12): word for word in every language. The old absolute wording ('Nobody ... admins included') is withdrawn.

security.admin_claim_operator.context: Last sentence of the admin claim, shown after security.admin_claim_setup_key. Keep it word for word in every language.

security.admin_claim_powers.context: Third sentence of the admin claim (after security.admin_claim_temp_password). CHANGED in batch 2b: it now also lists re-creating an address, moving aliases, and says the person is told when their two-factor sign-in is reset (the landing page says the same: 'the person is notified when their two-factor sign-in is reset'). Use the landing page's words for the same things. Word for word in every language.

security.admin_claim_setup_key.context: Fourth sentence of the admin claim, NEW in batch 2b. 'Setup key' is the deployment secret the person who deployed Edging Mail sets (APP_PASSWORD); it is the same term as in the Setup and break-glass screens (breakglass.setup_key). 'Console access' = being able to sign in to the admin console again. The restored admin gets a new key, so mail that arrived under the old key stays locked.

security.admin_claim_temp_password.context: Second sentence of the admin claim, always shown right after security.admin_claim_no_access. Final wording from the Product Owner (addendum 4.12): word for word in every language. 'Server key' is the key the server holds for mail that arrives before the person has signed in.

security.admin_delete_lost_keys.context: Delete account dialog: wording from the Product Owner, keep it word for word in every language.

security.cannot_turn_off_admin.context: Security card row 'Two-factor sign-in': shown instead of a Turn off button when the signed-in person is an admin.

security.cannot_turn_off_required.context: Security card row 'Two-factor sign-in': shown instead of a Turn off button when the organisation requires two-factor sign-in of everyone.

security.change_password.context: Button: Security card row 'Password' (opens the change-password form) and the submit button of that form.

security.codes_lead.context: Paragraph above the password and code fields of the 'Get new recovery codes' form: the old recovery codes stop working.

security.codes_replace_note.context: Shown above the new recovery codes list (after the form): the new codes replace the old ones.

security.current_password.context: Label of the first field of the change-password form: the password used now (the next two fields are the new one, gate.new_password and gate.repeat_password).

security.key_new_done.context: Success message after the new recovery key was stored, with a Back button under it.

security.key_new_lead.context: Paragraph above the password field that starts making a new recovery key: it replaces the old one, the password and the mail stay as they are.

security.key_test_button.context: Button: submits the typed recovery key to the test (no request is sent; the check runs in the browser).

security.key_test_hint.context: Hint under the recovery key test field: the shape of a recovery key (54 characters in nine groups of six).

security.key_test_lead.context: Paragraph above the recovery key test field: what the test does, that it runs in this browser and sends nothing.

security.key_test_ok.context: Result of the recovery key test when the key is the current one.

security.key_test_wrong.context: Result of the recovery key test when the key is well formed but is not the current one. Does not say how it differs.

security.new_codes.context: Button: Security card row 'Two-factor sign-in' (only when it is on): makes a new set of recovery codes; also the submit button of that form.

security.new_key.context: Button: Security card row 'Recovery key' (starts making a new recovery key that replaces the old one).

security.off_done.context: Success message after two-factor sign-in was turned off, with a Back button under it.

security.off_lead.context: Paragraph above the password and code fields of the form that turns two-factor sign-in off: says what is lost.

security.on_done.context: Success message after two-factor sign-in was turned on and the recovery codes were saved, with a Back button under it.

security.on_lead.context: Paragraph above the password field that starts turning on two-factor sign-in (the QR code screen follows).

security.other_devices_note.context: Note under the submit button of the new-recovery-codes and turn-off forms: this device stays signed in, every other device is signed out (the server ends the other sessions).

security.password_changed.context: Success message in Settings > Account > Security after the person changed their password, with a Back button under it. This device stays signed in; every other device was signed out. Plain sentence, no question mark.

security.password_note.context: Plain note under the Change password button: what changing the password does and does not do.

security.recovery_hint.context: Settings > Account > Security: line under the 'Recovery key' row label: what the recovery key is for (forgot-password flow keeps the mail readable).

security.status_off.context: Security card row 'Two-factor sign-in': status line when it is off.

security.status_on.context: Security card row 'Two-factor sign-in': status line when it is on.

security.step_up_lead.context: Shown above the new recovery key when the server asks for a code from the authenticator app first: tells the person to type the six-digit code in the field below it.

security.step_up_retry.context: Red error line under the new recovery key confirm button: the code field above must be filled, then the person confirms again.

security.test_key.context: Button: Security card row 'Recovery key' (opens the form that checks a typed recovery key, in the browser).

security.title.context: Heading of the Security card in Settings > Account (password, recovery key, two-factor sign-in).

security.turn_off.context: Button: Security card row 'Two-factor sign-in' (only when it is on and may be turned off); also the submit button of the form that turns it off.

security.turn_on.context: Button: Security card row 'Two-factor sign-in' (only when it is off): starts the enrolment.

send.changed_body.context: Body of that confirmation. Honest and calm: a changed key is normal after a person sets up their keys again, but it can also mean the key was replaced. 'Fingerprint' is a short number (6 groups of 5 digits) that identifies a key; the person can read it to the other one by phone or in person. Do not claim the key is safe or unsafe.

send.changed_confirm.context: Button of the key-changed confirmation: send, and remember the new key for this person. Not a question.

send.changed_line.context: One line block per person in that dialog: the address, then the fingerprint of the key used before ({before}) and of the new key ({now}); the fingerprints are groups of digits. Keep the three lines (separated by line breaks).

send.changed_title.context: Title of the confirmation shown when the encryption key of a recipient is not the one this browser remembered from earlier sends (key pinning, S3).

send.external_body.context: Body of that confirmation. {addresses} is one address per line. It must say the answer is sent without the protection of the message it answers (that message was encrypted in the sender's browser) and that quoted text leaves in the clear. Do not use the badge term 'end-to-end encrypted' here (a catalogue test allows it only on the e2e.badge keys). 'Edging Mail' is the product name and is never translated.

send.external_title.context: Title of the confirmation before answering or forwarding an end-to-end encrypted message to an address outside this Edging Mail (N6).

send.no_keys_body.context: Body of that confirmation. {addresses} is one address per line (one or several people); 'they' covers both. It must keep both facts: the server can read the message, and only until the person signs in and sets up encryption. Do not soften it into 'may'.

send.no_keys_inline.context: Extra paragraph in the confirmation before sending to a person who has not set up encryption yet (send.no_keys_body), shown only when the message has images placed inside the text. Their copy travels as plain text and loses the position of those images; they still receive the files. Calm, factual.

send.no_keys_title.context: Title of the confirmation before sending a message to a person on this Edging Mail who has never signed in (CK-1). Said calmly, not alarming.

send.send_anyway.context: Button that confirms sending although the situation in the dialog is not ideal (a recipient without keys, or a reply that leaves end-to-end encryption). Not a question.

send.too_big_body.context: Body of that confirmation: the message cannot be encrypted in the browser for everyone, so it can go the usual way, where the server can read it. Keep 'the server can read it' explicit.

send.too_big_confirm.context: Button that sends the message the usual way (not end-to-end encrypted). Not a question.

send.too_big_title.context: Title of the confirmation shown when a message is over the size limits of the end-to-end route (too large, too many files, too many recipients for the files).

send.was_keyed_body.context: Body of that confirmation. {addresses} is one address per line. Keep both consequences: the server can read the message, or it leaves as normal email. A legitimate cause exists (an admin deleted the keys, the account was re-created).

send.was_keyed_title.context: Title of the confirmation before sending to an address this browser sent ENCRYPTED mail to before, when the server now says it has no encryption keys or is not on this server (EC-2).

settings.address_hint.context: Settings, Account tab: grey hint under the read-only address field. It says the address is the sign-in name and the sender address and cannot be changed (security review CAT-4).

settings.admin_hint.context: Settings, Account tab (admins only): description inside the Admin console card.

settings.appearance.context: Settings, Account tab: title of the Appearance card (a Language row will be added there by another batch).

settings.dark_theme.context: Settings, Account tab: label of the dark-theme on/off switch.

settings.display_name_placeholder.context: Settings, Account tab: placeholder of the Display name field.

settings.load_failed.context: Settings, Account tab: red message when the settings could not be loaded.

settings.open_admin.context: Settings, Account tab (admins only): button inside the Admin console card.

settings.push_blocked.context: Settings, Notifications card: red status line when the browser has blocked notifications for the site.

settings.push_device.context: Settings, Account tab, Notifications card: label of the switch that turns new-mail notifications on or off for this device.

settings.push_off.context: Settings, Notifications card: status line under the switch label when notifications are off.

settings.push_on.context: Settings, Notifications card: status line under the switch label when notifications are on.

settings.push_test.context: Settings, Notifications card: button that sends a test notification to this device.

settings.push_unsupported.context: Settings, Notifications card: shown when the browser cannot do notifications. {brand} is the product name (not translated).

settings.push_working.context: Settings, Notifications card: status line under the switch label while it is being changed.

settings.save_offline.context: Settings, Account tab: red message when saving failed because the device is offline.

settings.saved.context: Settings, Account tab: green confirmation next to the Save button.

setup.address_hint.context: First-run Setup screen, step 1: small hint under the email address field (the label is auth.email_label). It is the first admin's sign-in address.

setup.err_address_invalid.context: First-run Setup screen, step 1: red text under the address field when it is not an address the app can host: only letters, digits and the three characters . _ - are allowed before the @. Keep the example and the characters as they are.

setup.err_address_required.context: First-run Setup screen, step 1: red text under the address field when it is empty.

setup.err_key_required.context: First-run Setup screen, step 1: red text under the setup key field when it is empty.

setup.err_name_invalid.context: First-run Setup screen, step 1: red text under the display name field when it has a line break or is too long. {max} is the longest allowed length in characters (100).

setup.key_hint.context: First-run Setup screen, step 1: small hint under the setup key field. Plain words for the APP_PASSWORD deployment secret; do not translate it as a password to sign in with.

setup.key_label.context: First-run Setup screen, step 1: label of the field for the setup key, a secret the person who deployed the app chose.

setup.lead.context: First-run Setup screen, step 1: one sentence under the heading. The account being created is the first admin.

setup.name_hint.context: First-run Setup screen, step 1: small hint under the display name field (the label is term.display_name). The field may stay empty.

setup.not_ready_app_password.context: First-run Setup screen when the deployment lacks secrets: shown only when APP_PASSWORD is in the list. Says that this secret is the setup key asked for on the next screen. Keep APP_PASSWORD untranslated.

setup.not_ready_lead.context: First-run Setup screen when the deployment lacks secrets: one sentence under the heading. The names of the missing secrets follow as code-styled labels.

setup.not_ready_list.context: First-run Setup screen when the deployment lacks secrets: caption above the list of missing secret names (JWT_SECRET, APP_PASSWORD, DATA_KEY).

setup.not_ready_next.context: First-run Setup screen when the deployment lacks secrets: what to do next (add the secrets as the deployment guide describes), then the Reload button.

setup.not_ready_title.context: First-run Setup screen when the deployment lacks secrets: heading of the card that replaces the form.

setup.reload.context: Button: reloads the page after the missing secrets were added (first-run Setup screen).

setup.step.context: First-run Setup screen: small centred line above each step. {current} is the step number (1 or 2) and {total} the number of steps (2).

setup.title.context: First-run Setup screen, step 1: heading of the card (shown before any account exists).

setup.wrong_key_retry.context: First-run Setup, step 2 (the recovery key screen): hint under a field to type the setup key again after the server refused it. Nothing was created, so the recovery key shown above is still valid; the person does not start again.

sidebar.close_mailboxes.context: Screen-reader label of the X button of the phone folder drawer

snooze.this_weekend.context: Snooze menu item: wake up on Saturday morning

snooze.tomorrow.context: Snooze menu item: wake up tomorrow morning

snooze.tomorrow_at.context: Wake-up time written out when it is tomorrow; {time} is a clock time such as 8:00 AM. Spaces are made non-breaking by the code

snooze.too_far.context: Error in the snooze date picker when the time is more than a year away

snooze.too_soon.context: Error in the snooze date picker when the time is less than a minute away

snooze.until.context: Small chip on a snoozed message row; {when} is a day and time such as tomorrow 8:00 AM, about 18 characters

time.yesterday.context: Time cell of a message-list row received yesterday (the group headings of the list are list.group_*)

toast.archived.context: Toast after a message was archived (has an Undo button)

toast.deleted_forever.context: Toast after a message was deleted for good (no Undo)

toast.moved_back_to_inbox.context: Toast after a snoozed message was brought back to the Inbox now

toast.moved_to_inbox.context: Toast after a message was restored from Trash or Spam to the Inbox

toast.moved_to_spam.context: Toast after a message was moved to Spam (has an Undo button)

toast.moved_to_trash.context: Toast after a message was moved to Trash (has an Undo button)

toast.snoozed_until.context: Toast after a message was snoozed; {when} is a date text such as 'tomorrow 8:00 AM' (has an Undo button)

twofa.code_hint.context: Two-factor enrolment screen: small hint under the six-digit code input (codes change every 30 seconds).

twofa.code_label.context: Two-factor enrolment screen: label of the input where the person types the six-digit code the authenticator app shows.

twofa.codes_keep.context: Recovery codes panel, under the Copy and Download buttons: keep the codes somewhere safe; they are shown only this once.

twofa.codes_lead.context: Recovery codes panel: what the codes are for (signing in when the phone with the authenticator app is lost) and that each works once.

twofa.codes_not_key.context: Recovery codes panel: says plainly that these codes are not the recovery key and cannot restore mail. Keep the two glossary terms (recovery codes, recovery key) as two different things in every language.

twofa.codes_title.context: Recovery codes panel (shown once after two-factor sign-in is turned on): heading of the panel. The recovery codes are single-use codes for two-factor sign-in, never the recovery key.

twofa.continue.context: Button: last button of the recovery codes panel, enabled once the checkbox is ticked; leaves the two-factor setup.

twofa.copy_failed.context: Red alert under a Copy button (the manual key on the enrolment screen, or the recovery codes) when the browser refused to copy.

twofa.download.context: Button: next to Copy in the recovery codes panel; saves the codes as a text file named edging-mail-recovery-codes.txt.

twofa.file_note.context: Last line of the downloaded recovery codes text file (the title above it already says recovery codes): each recovery code works once, and what it is for. cyber CAT-18: zh must say 恢复码, not 代码.

twofa.file_title.context: First line of the downloaded recovery codes text file (file name edging-mail-recovery-codes.txt). Keep the product name Edging Mail unchanged.

twofa.intro.context: Two-factor enrolment screen (first sign-in gate, or Settings), paragraph under the card title, above the QR code: what two-factor sign-in is and what an authenticator app does.

twofa.manual_title.context: Two-factor enrolment screen: label above the text key (base32 secret, shown in groups of four) for a person who cannot scan the QR code.

twofa.qr_failed.context: Two-factor enrolment screen: red alert in place of the QR code when the code could not be drawn; the manual key below it still works.

twofa.qr_label.context: Accessible name (aria-label) of the QR code image on the two-factor enrolment screen; read by screen readers, not shown.

twofa.saved_check.context: Recovery codes panel: label of the required checkbox that enables the Continue button.

twofa.saved_hint.context: Recovery codes panel: small text under the 'I have saved these recovery codes' checkbox.

twofa.scan_lead.context: Two-factor enrolment screen: instruction line directly above the QR code.

twofa.verify.context: Button: primary button under the six-digit code input on the two-factor enrolment screen; checks the code and turns two-factor sign-in on.

users.alias_heading.context: Account dialog: heading of the section that lists the extra addresses (aliases) of the person.

users.alias_hint.context: Account dialog: explains what an extra address does.

users.alias_none.context: Account dialog: the person has no extra address.

users.alias_placeholder.context: Placeholder of the extra address field: an example address.

users.alias_remove.context: aria-label of the icon-only X button that removes one extra address. {address} is that extra address.

users.confirm_reissue.context: Confirmation paragraph before a new temporary password is issued. {hours} is a number (72 today).

users.confirm_reset_two_factor.context: Account dialog: confirmation text before an admin resets a person's two-factor sign-in.

users.copy_failed.context: Temporary password dialog: shown next to the Copy button when the browser refused to copy.

users.create_account.context: Button that submits the New account dialog.

users.create_domains_failed.context: New account dialog: the list of domains could not be loaded (a Try again button follows).

users.create_name_hint.context: New account dialog: hint under the display name field.

users.create_no_domain.context: New account dialog: no domain exists yet, so no account can be created.

users.create_password_note.context: New account dialog: tells the admin what happens after Create account.

users.created_give.context: Temporary password dialog: first sentence. {address} is the new account's address (shown in bold).

users.created_note_expiry.context: Temporary password dialog: second bullet under the password (how long the temporary password is valid). {hours} is a number (72 today).

users.created_note_once.context: Temporary password dialog: first bullet under the password.

users.created_note_send.context: Temporary password dialog: third bullet under the password.

users.created_title.context: Title of the dialog that shows the temporary password of a new account.

users.creating.context: Button label of the New account dialog while the account is being created.

users.delete_body.context: Delete account dialog: first paragraph. {address} is the account's address (shown in bold).

users.delete_confirm_label.context: Delete account dialog: label of the field where the admin types the exact address.

users.delete_key_note.context: Delete account dialog: second sentence under the Product Owner text, about the new key of a re-created account.

users.delete_title.context: Title of the confirmation dialog before an account is deleted.

users.deleting.context: Button label of the Delete account dialog while the account is being deleted.

users.empty.context: Admin People tab when there is no account at all.

users.err_local_dots.context: Form error under the address field: the part before the @ has a misplaced dot.

users.err_local_empty.context: Form error under the address field of the New account dialog: nothing typed before the @.

users.extra_addresses#other.context: User list row: how many extra addresses (aliases) the account has. {count} is a number.

users.last_sign_in.context: User list row: when the person last signed in. {when} is a date and time already formatted for the language.

users.loading.context: Admin People tab while the list loads (spinner and text).

users.make_member.context: Button in the account dialog (and its confirm button): gives an admin the member role.

users.never_signed_in.context: User list row: the person has not signed in yet.

users.new_account.context: Button above the people list, and title of the dialog it opens.

users.no_match.context: Admin People tab when a search finds nobody. {query} is the text the admin searched for.

users.not_signed_in_yet.context: Badge in the account dialog: the person has never signed in with their own password and has no keys yet (the only state in which an admin can issue a new temporary password).

users.password_saved.context: Button that closes the temporary password dialog (the only way to close it).

users.role.context: New account dialog: legend of the radio group that picks Member or Admin.

users.save_name.context: Button next to the display name field of the account dialog.

users.search_label.context: aria-label of the search field of the People tab. Screen reader only.

users.search_placeholder.context: Placeholder of the search field of the People tab.

users.self_note.context: Account dialog, own account: why the disable, delete and reset buttons are missing.

users.showing.context: Admin People tab under the list: how many accounts are loaded of how many exist. {shown} and {total} are numbers.

users.status_active.context: Badge in the account dialog: the account is active.

users.status_disabled.context: Badge on an account that is disabled (user list row and account dialog).
